name: PLATO ASU Optimization Benchmarks
description: The PLATO (Planning and Logistics Algorithm Testing and Optimization) benchmark suite, hosted by Arizona State University's Decision Tree Labs, provides a comprehensive collection of test instances for mathematical programming solvers across a wide range of problem types. The suite covers linear programming (LP), mixed-integer linear programming (MILP), semidefinite programming (SDP), second-order cone programming (SOCP), nonlinear programming (NLP), quadratic programming (QP), mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP), and mathematical programs with equilibrium constraints (MPEC). Benchmarks are used to compare commercial and open-source optimization software on feasibility, optimality, and robustness.
typical_sota_score: Varies widely by problem class; leading solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, MOSEK) typically dominate across LP, MILP, and SOCP categories.
reputation: Well-regarded resource in the operations research community; used by solver developers and researchers to compare performance across a broad spectrum of optimization problem classes.
notes: Not an LLM benchmark; targets mathematical optimization solvers. Results tables are regularly updated as new solver versions are released. Covers both feasibility and optimization variants. Some benchmark categories focus on pathological or infeasible instances.
